Add the Kidney Donor Risk Index and Kidney Donor Profile Index

Source: R/add_kdpi.R
add_kdpi.Rd

Computes the donor-only Kidney Donor Risk Index (KDRI) and the Kidney Donor Profile Index (KDPI) for deceased kidney donors from Standard Analysis File (SAF) columns, and appends three columns: the unscaled KDRI (KDRI_RAO), the KDRI scaled to the median donor of the reference year (KDRI), and the KDPI, a percentile from 0 to 100.

Usage

add_kdpi(
  df,
  version = c("refit2024", "rao2009"),
  table = "latest",
  unknown_history = c("optn", "na"),
  kdri_rao_col = "KDRI_RAO",
  kdri_col = "KDRI",
  kdpi_col = "KDPI",
  return_terms = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

A data frame of deceased donors or transplants, one row each.

version

KDRI formula: "refit2024" (default) or "rao2009".

table

Which mapping table to use: "latest" (default), the newest stored table for version; "in_force", for each row the table OPTN was using on DON_RECOV_DT; or a table label such as "2018" (see optn_mapping_tables). For "in_force", each table's start date is OPTN's published date where one exists (2024-05-29, the refit on 2024-10-31, and 2025-05-21); otherwise it is June 1 of the year after the reference year, the deadline OPTN Policy 8.4.B sets, which is a convention. Rao 2009 tables end on 2024-10-31 and refit tables start then. Rows with no stored table in force, such as refit KDPI from 2025-05-21, when OPTN used a table it has not archived, get a missing KDPI, with a warning. The dates and their basis are in optn_mapping_tables$effective.

unknown_history

How to treat unknown hypertension or diabetes history (code 998). "optn" (default) follows the OPTN calculator: the term is weighted by the share of reference donors with that history, printed on the mapping table. The 2012 and 2013 tables do not print these shares, so with them unknown history gives a missing KDRI. "na" always gives a missing KDRI.

kdri_rao_col, kdri_col, kdpi_col

Names of the output columns.

return_terms

If TRUE, also add a list-column KDRI_terms with each row's linear predictor components.

Value

df with three new columns. The KDPI column carries attributes optn_table (the table label used for each row) and kdri_formula.

Details

Two formulas are available. "refit2024" is the formula OPTN has used since 2024-10-31, refit without donor race or hepatitis C. "rao2009" is the original 10-factor donor-only formula, used by OPTN before then. The KDPI comes from an OPTN mapping table (see optn_mapping_tables); only tables built with the chosen formula are used.

Input columns (codes as in the SRTR data dictionary; labelled factors from apply_srtr_factors() also work):

  • DON_AGE (years), DON_HGT_CM, DON_WGT_KG, DON_CREAT (mg/dL);

  • DON_HIST_HYPERTEN, DON_HIST_DIAB: 1 no, 2 to 5 yes, 998 unknown;

  • DON_CAD_DON_COD (2 = cerebrovascular/stroke; 1, 3, 4, 999 = other; 998 = unknown), or DON_COD_DON_STROKE (1 = yes, 0 = no) when DON_CAD_DON_COD is absent;

  • DON_NON_HR_BEAT (Y = donation after circulatory death);

  • for "rao2009" only: DON_RACE_BLACK_AFRICAN_AMERICAN (Y/N), or DON_RACE (16 = Black or African American; 1024 = unknown) when that column is absent; and at least one of DON_ANTI_HCV, DON_HCV_NAT (P = positive) and DON_HCV_STAT (1 = positive);

  • for table = "in_force": DON_RECOV_DT.

As in the OPTN calculator, creatinine above 8 mg/dL counts as 8, and for "rao2009" an unknown, pending or not-done HCV result counts as negative. Any other missing or unknown input, including an unknown cause of death or race and a creatinine that is not a positive number, gives a missing KDRI and KDPI. A multiracial donor (a DON_RACE code that is a sum of single codes) is not counted as Black by the DON_RACE fallback.

References

Rao PS, Schaubel DE, Guidinger MK, et al. A comprehensive risk quantification score for deceased donor kidneys: the kidney donor risk index. Transplantation 2009;88:231-236. doi:10.1097/TP.0b013e3181ac620b

OPTN. A Guide to Calculating and Interpreting the Kidney Donor Profile Index (KDPI). Updated 2020-03-23 (Table 1, Rao 2009 coefficients) and 2026-04-23 (Table 1, refit coefficients).

Examples

donors <- data.frame(
  DON_AGE = c(52, 30),
  DON_HGT_CM = c(183, 165),
  DON_WGT_KG = c(81, 70),
  DON_HIST_HYPERTEN = c(2, 1),
  DON_HIST_DIAB = c(1, 1),
  DON_CAD_DON_COD = c(2, 3),
  DON_CREAT = c(1.7, 0.9),
  DON_NON_HR_BEAT = c("Y", "N")
)
add_kdpi(donors)
#>   DON_AGE DON_HGT_CM DON_WGT_KG DON_HIST_HYPERTEN DON_HIST_DIAB DON_CAD_DON_COD
#> 1      52        183         81                 2             1               2
#> 2      30        165         70                 1             1               3
#>   DON_CREAT DON_NON_HR_BEAT  KDRI_RAO      KDRI KDPI
#> 1       1.7               Y 1.7123557 1.1749559   67
#> 2       0.9               N 0.9813462 0.6733639   13
